The commit is fleet.yml's sourceCommit for billing, and billing's tree was verifiably AT it (clean, HEAD) when this was transcribed.
title: billing.payment.failed payload
description: The `data` payload of the `billing.payment.failed` event: a charge attempt was declined or errored. Only the invoice-backed shape exists for this type — a failed Checkout session is not a payment event, so unlike `billing.payment.succeeded` this schema has no second form. `amount` is what could **not** be collected, never what was: a failed charge that reported `amount_paid` would reconcile a decline as a settled zero, which is the specific bug the publisher's own comment warns about. **The recipient fact, added 2026-10-07 (core-w46): `email` is the customer's billing address, and it is OPTIONAL and NEVER NULL** — billing's `StripeEvents.with_recipient` merges it only when `customers.email` is present, so a decline for a customer with no address on file arrives without it. Optional and non-nullable for the same reason as on `billing.payment.succeeded`: required would reject a real event, and nullable would promise a shape billing never sends. The envelope is validated by schemas/event-envelope.schema.json; this schema validates what is inside `data`. The file path is the event type with dots as directory separators. See docs/event-naming.md.

processor_event_id.description: The processor's own event id for the webhook this came from, e.g. `evt_…`. Retries of the same decline arrive with the same processor event id and different envelope ids, so this is what a consumer deduplicates on — not the envelope's `id`.

customer_id.description: The processor's customer id, e.g. `cus_…`. Present on a failure for the same reason it is present on a success: a decline is only actionable if somebody can be told.

invoice_id.description: The processor's invoice id, e.g. `in_…`, whose collection attempt failed. The identity of the charge that did not happen.

amount.description: What could **not** be collected, in integer minor units and a currency. The amount due, not the amount paid — on a failed charge the latter is a zero that means "nothing was collected", and a consumer reading it as the charge size reconciles a declined 29.00 as a settled 0.00.

amount_minor.description: Amount due and not collected, in the currency's minor units.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code, uppercase, normalised on the way in.

subscription_id.description: The processor's subscription id, e.g. `sub_…`, or null when the invoice was not for a subscription. When present it is also the envelope's `subject`; when null the subject falls back to the customer id.

payment_intent_id.description: The processor's payment intent, e.g. `pi_…`, or null when the attempt failed without one. What a support conversation needs to look up.

paid.description: The processor's settled flag for the invoice, `false` for this type. Not constrained to `false` in the schema: a partial payment followed by a failed retry is a real state, and a schema that refused it would reject a real event rather than a fake one.

attempt_count.description: How many times the processor has attempted this invoice, or null. The number a retry policy keys on, and the difference between "declined once" and "declined five times and the card is dead".

next_payment_attempt.description: RFC3339 UTC when the processor will retry, or null when it will not. Non-null here is the start of the grace period that `billing.subscription.past_due` announces.

email.description: The customer's billing email, or ABSENT — never null — when there is no address to carry. billing's `StripeEvents.with_recipient` resolves it from the processor's customer id by one indexed lookup on `customers.processor_customer_id` and merges it only when `customers.email` is present: a customer created in the processor's dashboard has no cafaye row, and one created through `/v1` has no email until the client sets one. Optional and non-nullable for that reason: required would reject every event for a customer with no address, and nullable would promise a shape billing never sends. Named `email` to match identity's events, which carry the same fact for the same reason — one fleet, one field name for the address a consumer cannot look up.
